newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - MetLife aims to gain on Prudential.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - MetLife aims to gain on Prudential.

text.p: Its merger with New England Mutual Life Insurance Co completed, Metropolitan Life Insurance Co now plans to turn its attention to overtaking Prudential Insurance Co of America as the largest U.S. life insurer.

"Together we want to be the leader in providing financial security for people through life insurance, investment products, mutual funds, annuities, and some other areas" MetLife chairman Harry Kamen told Reuters in a telephone interview with Kamen and New England chairman Robert Shafto.
Prudential currently ranks as that largest U.S. life insurer with insurance assets of $187 billion. Metropolitan ranks second with assets, after the merger, of about $159 billion.
Kamen said MetLife wants to be the leader by moving "ahead of Prudential."
Metropolitan plans to continue its focus on middle income and institutional markets while New England concentrates on the upscale market.

But, "with the Met's ratings, name and reputation, the brand name that they bring to the table, along with the New England maintaining our identity as New England Life, we feel we can penetrate those markets successfully," Shafto said.
Shafto said sales are up more than 10 percent year to date and August sales were up over 30 percent compared to a year ago and compared to an industry with flat-to-weaker sales.
"We're doing well and the merger is what's making that transition work for us," Shafto said.
Kamen said he expects the rating agencies this week to
raise New England's claims-paying ability ratings to match MetLife's double A rating.
Although the companies pursued the merger for strategic marketing purposes, it will produce some cost savings, Kamen said.
He said he expects about $30 million to $50 million in cost savings from the merger.
With regulatory, legal and financial hurdles out of the way, Shafto said the two companies are now working to integrate their operations and further develop their common goals.

"We're working with the Met to develop some computer systems," Shafto said. And, he said, "We're working on a plan for a common computer platform to support both companies' product development," he said.
"The devil's in the details," Shafto said.
